newsitem.title: USA: New Nirvana album opens at top of U.S. charts. [CORRECTED 02:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: New Nirvana album opens at top of U.S. charts. [CORRECTED 02:55 GMT]

text.p: A posthumous album of performances by Nirvana opened at the top of the U.S. album charts, narrowly beating a new release by another hard rock band, Tool, according to sales data released on Wednesday.

"From the Muddy Banks of the Wishkah" (Corrects from "From the Mighty Banks of the Wishkah"), which consists of 17 songs recorded at various Nirvana concerts between 1989 and 1994, sold almost 159,000 copies in the week ended October 6, said the band's Geffen Records label. Geffen is a unit of Seagram Co Ltd's MCA Records. After Nirvana vocalist Kurt Cobain killed himself in April 1994, Geffen released the band's "MTV Unplugged In New York" in November of that year.
It opened at number one with sales of more than 310,000. On this week's charts, Nirvana's major-label breakthrough "Nevermind", re-entered at 192, more than five years after it was released.
Opening in number two this week was "Aenima" from Los Angeles rock band Tool, with sales of almost 148,000, according to the group's label Zoo Entertainment.
Celine Dion's "Falling Into You" slipped to third after two weeks at number one. Her album is released by Epic Records, a unit of Sony Corp.
Two other new entries in the top 10 were "Moment" at number four from saxophonist Kenny G. on Bertelsmann AG's Arista Records; and Luther Vandross' "Your Secret Love" at nine on Epic.

Three high profile new releases lost their standing in the top 10 this week. Sheryl Crow's self-titled second album fell to 13 after opening at six last week. The album is released by PolyGram NV's A&M Records.

In its fourth week on the charts, R.E.M.'s "New Adventures in Hi-Fi" slid to 17 from seven the week before. The album is released by Time Warner Inc's Warner Bros. Records, that recently signed an $80 million contract with the band for six more albums. Warner Bros, one of the largest labels in the U.S., handles only one other album in the top 50, Alanis Morissette's eight-placed "Jagged Little Pill", still going strong after 69 weeks.

Pearl Jam's fourth Epic Records album, "No Code", fell to 20 from 10 in its sixth week. The album has sold just over 790,000 copies to date. By contrast, the band's previous release, "Vitalogy", sold 877,000 copies in its first week when it was released in 1994.
